key_insight: Across nine metals, predicted direct hot-electron injection into adsorbed CO exceeds hot-hole injection because the CO LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi level than the HOMO.
engineering_relevance: Metal selection and adsorbate orbital alignment offer design levers for nanoscale photocatalysts that transfer charge before hot carriers thermalize.
method: Model CO–metal interactions using ab initio density functional theory.
Describe localized surface plasmons using macroscopic electrodynamics.
Predict electron and hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles.
evidence_signal: Calculations across Ag, Au, Cu, Al, Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir and Pt identify Al, Ag, Cu and Au as the strongest electron injectors at optical photon energies, with significant plasmonic enhancement for Cu and Au.
watch_item: The predictions concern CO on large spherical nanoparticles; transferability to other adsorbates and particle geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
